column3: After five days the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a certain attorney named Tertullus, who presented their case against Paul to the governor.
And when he had been summoned, Tertullus began accusing him, saying, “Because through you we enjoy great peace, and reforms are happening for this nation through your foresight,
we welcome this in every way and everywhere, most excellent Felix, with all gratitude.
But so that I may not detain you any further, I ask you to hear us briefly in your kindness.
For we found this man a plague, stirring up rebellion among all the Jews throughout the inhabited world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes,
who even tried to profane the temple, and we seized him.
From him you yourself will be able, by examining him, to learn about all these things of which we accuse him.”
The Jews also joined in the attack, affirming that these things were so.
And when the governor nodded for him to speak, Paul answered: “Knowing that you have been a judge over this nation for many years, I cheerfully make my defense concerning myself.
You are able to verify that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem to worship.
And they did not find me in the temple disputing with anyone or causing a crowd to gather, either in the synagogues or throughout the city.
Nor are they able to prove to you the things of which they now accuse me.
But I confess this to you, that according to the Way which they call a sect, in this way I serve the God of our fathers, believing all the things according to the law and written in the prophets,
having hope toward God, which these men themselves also accept, that there is going to be a resurrection of both the righteous and the unrighteous.
In this I myself also strive always to have an unoffending conscience toward God and people.
Now after many years I came bringing alms to my nation and offerings,
in which they found me purified in the temple, not with a crowd or disturbance.
But there were some Jews from Asia who ought to be present before you and accuse me if they have anything against me.
Or let these men themselves say what wrongdoing they found when I stood before the council,
except concerning this one voice that I cried out while standing among them: ‘Concerning resurrection of the dead I am being judged before you today.’”
But Felix, having a more accurate knowledge concerning the Way, postponed them, saying, “When Lysias the commander comes down, I will decide your case.”
And he ordered the centurion to keep him in custody but to give him some freedom, and to prevent none of his own people from attending to him.
Now after some days Felix arrived with Drusilla his wife, who was Jewish, and he sent for Paul and listened to him concerning faith in Christ Jesus.
But as he reasoned about righteousness and self-control and the coming judgment, Felix became afraid and answered, “Go away for now; when I find an opportunity, I will summon you.”
At the same time he was also hoping that money would be given to him by Paul. Therefore he was sending for him more frequently and conversing with him.
But when two years were completed, Felix received Porcius Festus as successor. And wanting to gain favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul bound.
